calls.head: Where the Canadiens have the edge: shot quality
calls.body: The Canadiens are the league’s best for shot quality, and the Predators are near the bottom. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Canadiens’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Predators’.

calls.title: Montréal got the better looks
calls.plain: The Canadiens came out clearly ahead on shot quality, as the gap between these two suggested.
calls.said: the Canadiens would get better looks than the Predators
calls.beyond: Montréal usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Nashville’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% (about 6.4% against Montréal) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

story.head: Kerfoot sparks a Predators comeback
paras: The first goal of the game would have been Montréal’s, but it was taken off for offside a little over a minute in. They got it back early in the second, when Nick Suzuki officially opened the scoring. Alex Newhook stretched the lead to 2-0 midway through the period, but that’s where Montréal’s luck ran out. The Predators’ Mavrik Bourque left in the second period and didn’t return. Alexander Kerfoot scored his first goal for Nashville late in the period to get the Predators on the board. Matthew Wood made it 2-2 on the power play less than five minutes later. Ryan O'Reilly put the Predators ahead on the power play to complete the comeback with a little over three minutes left. Adam Edström then scored into the empty net twice in the last three minutes, the first of them his first goal for Nashville, and it finished 5-2.

The score flatters the Predators: the Canadiens had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Habs win about seven in ten. Juuse Saros was the difference, stopping 31 of 33. Jacob Fowler stopped 15 of 18 for the Canadiens.

The power plays decided it: Wood and O'Reilly both scored on the power play as the Predators turned a two-goal hole into the lead, and the Canadiens went 0-for-3 on theirs. Arber Xhekaj picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Predators moved to 2-1-1, and the Canadiens fell to 1-2-1.
